overview: This House resolution sets the ground rules for House debate on H.R. 4, a bill to cancel certain federal funding that the President asked Congress to rescind, or take back, in messages sent on June 3, 2025. Under the Impoundment Control Act of 1974, a President can propose canceling funds Congress already approved, and Congress has a limited time to agree. The resolution allows one hour of debate split between the Majority Leader and Minority Leader, waives procedural objections, and allows no amendments, only a single motion to recommit (send the bill back to committee). It also sets aside a section of that law that normally governs how such rescission bills are handled, and adopts another pending House resolution, H. Res. 492. The House adopted it on June 11, 2025.
for: Supporters say the rule lets the House take a quick, straightforward vote on the President's proposed spending cuts within the time limits set by law.
against: Critics say blocking all amendments and setting aside the normal rescission procedures limits members' ability to change which funds are cut, on a bill that cancels money Congress already approved.
